title: HeadRollback: Post-Task Attention Head Rollback for Replay-Free Continual LoRA Fine-Tuning

contributions.purpose: Mitigate catastrophic forgetting in continual LoRA fine-tuning without replay buffers or altered training.
contributions.mechanism: HeadRollback, a replay-free post-task intervention that rolls back the LoRA B-matrix rows of unintentionally disrupted attention heads to the previous checkpoint at task boundaries.
contributions.evaluation: Operates entirely at task boundaries with minimal state (one scalar per head plus a single checkpoint); no separate metric for this contribution itself.
contributions.source_quote: We propose HeadRollback, a replay-free post-task intervention for continual LoRA fine-tuning that operates at task boundaries without modifying training dynamics.

contributions.purpose: Decide which attention heads to preserve versus roll back.
contributions.mechanism: A three-signal scoring formula combining disruption magnitude, historical importance, and new-task importance.
contributions.evaluation: Used to identify heads worth preserving; effectiveness validated via the main benchmark results.
contributions.source_quote: We develop a three-signal scoring formula combining disruption magnitude, historical importance, and new-task importance to identify heads worth preserving.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate HeadRollback's effectiveness over vanilla continual LoRA.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluate on a 5-task text classification benchmark with Qwen3-0.6B-Base across multiple task orders.
contributions.evaluation: Improves Overall Performance by +1.98pp and Backward Transfer by +1.70pp over Vanilla LoRA, with 7/9 win rate across task orders.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that HeadRollback improves Overall Performance by +1.98pp and Backward Transfer by +1.70pp over Vanilla LoRA on a 5-task benchmark, with consistent improvements across task orders (7/9 win rate).

contributions.purpose: Explain what HeadRollback selects and where disruption occurs.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis comparing three-signal selection against disruption-only selection and inspecting per-layer susceptibility.
contributions.evaluation: Selected heads have 3-7x higher historical importance than disruption-only selection; middle layers are most susceptible to unintentional disruption.
contributions.source_quote: We provide analysis showing that HeadRollback selects heads with 3-7x higher historical importance than disruption-only selection, and that middle layers are most susceptible to unintentional disruption.

self_declared_provenance.quote: HeadRollback differs fundamentally as a post-task intervention that operates at task boundaries without modifying training dynamics or requiring replay data.
These methods modify the training process itself, whereas HeadRollback operates on trained LoRA modules as a post-hoc correction.

HeadRollback builds on this insight by using gradient-based importance signals to identify heads that were unintentionally disrupted, then selectively rolling back their LoRA parameters without requiring replay or distillation.

notes: Positive-result method paper; modest gains (+1.98pp / +1.70pp) but 7/9 (not 9/9) win rate across task orders, i.e., 2 task orders where it does not win.
